- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.2) or shows recent volatility, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price is trending up.
- If model shows a sharp spike in forecast followed by a drop, it often overcorrects; cap the peak and smooth the descent.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in the first 5–7 days of a new 30d horizon; apply a small upward bias early in the forecast.
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from positive to negative), model often fails to adjust; delay or reduce forecast increase until sentiment stabilizes.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon; if forecast is > 1.5σ above recent mean, reduce by 10–20% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- Overshoots after spikes are common; if forecast exceeds true outcome by > 1.2x in 3–5 days, apply a downward correction curve.
